_comment: Provisioner-worker config for the local demo stack (Workstream F).
WHY this file starts with an EMPTY backends list:
Backend IDs are server-generated (domain.NewID("b") -> random b_<uuid>);
the backend-create API ignores any client-supplied id. So the real IDs
only exist AFTER dev/seed.sh registers the backends. The worker's DBA
lookup is keyed by that backend ID (ephemeral.NewConfigDBALookup), so a
statically-pinned id here would never match.
dev/seed.sh REWRITES this file in place with the real backend IDs once it
has registered the backends, then you restart the worker to pick it up:
docker compose -f dev/compose.yml restart provisioner-worker
This committed stub keeps the worker boot-able BEFORE the first seed:
loadFile() requires worker_key_ref but tolerates an empty backends list,
so the worker starts, idles, and self-heals on the post-seed restart.
DBA creds are referenced as env:// (resolved by the secrets package), never
inlined: the dev backend root passwords are injected into the worker service
in dev/compose.yml. Local-demo values only.
worker_key_ref: 32-byte HMAC seed for deterministic ephemeral-credential
derivation (worker-only, distinct from SECRETBOX_KEY). Fixed dev value set
via WORKER_HMAC_KEY in the worker service.
BOTH demo workers share THIS one file (all three backends), so each can
resolve DBA creds + health-probe its slice; which backends a worker actually
claims + probes is set per-worker by WORKER_INSTANCE_WHITELIST (worker-1.env /
worker-2.env, also written by seed.sh): worker-1 = mysql+postgres, worker-2 =
mongo. The per-instance heartbeat health map thus covers pg+mysql+mongo across
the two workers.
